key_insight: Polygenic risk scores built from brain cell-type gene sets capture substantial and partly shared genetic risk across neurodegenerative diseases, with Alzheimer’s showing the broadest cell-type associations.
clinical_relevance: These results may help refine genetic stratification of neurodegenerative disease subtypes, especially dementia-related presentations, but they are not yet a standalone clinical tool.
method: Analyzed UK Biobank polygenic risk scores across multiple neurodegenerative diseases.
Restricted PRS construction to genes reported in microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and neurons.
Compared cell-type-based scores and APOE effects across disease phenotypes and dementia status.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, cell-type-specific PRSs explained about 60–93% of genetic liability for neurodegenerative diseases where dementia is a major clinical feature, and the authors report 21–29% overlap among cell-type gene sets.
watch_item: Current cell-type annotations overlap substantially, so PRS signals may not cleanly map to distinct brain cell biology and should be interpreted cautiously.
paper_title: Mapping polygenic risk scores to brain cells: insights for neurodegenerative diseases
